SMTO-CTX-0012 — SMTO asked for an attached file in two different sizes

GUID: 8b934587-39b5-4fe6-906b-88103cfd8de8
Slug: context-read-conflicting-limits
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: ctx

What happened

  • While reading a file you attached, SMTO gave two different size limits at once, one in letters and one in bytes, so the read was refused. Nothing was read and the file is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep going for a step or two. SMTO sees this message and usually asks again with a single size.
  2. If it repeats, open Agent Checks in the message box and, under Context & Attachments, turn on Read full attached context. With full reading on, SMTO ignores both sizes and reads the rest of the file.
  3. Then tell SMTO in the conversation: "Read the attached file again." This starts a fresh read that uses the new setting.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's next steps show text from the attached file.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't attach the same file again; the file isn't the problem.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A read_context call supplied both max_characters and the deprecated byte limit; read_source cannot apply two units as one cap (conflicting_limits).

What this means

  • A bounded read supplied both max_characters and the deprecated byte limit; the reader cannot apply two different units as one requested cap. Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • A bounded read supplied both max_characters and the deprecated byte limit; the reader cannot apply two different units as one requested cap.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the read arguments for both max_characters and limit; the full-read policy has different handling and does not turn a byte count into characters.

How to fix it

  • Supply exactly one of max_characters or the deprecated limit argument to read_context (native/context_reads.py read_source). With read_full_attached_context enabled, both amount arguments are ignored.
  • Supply max_characters or the deprecated byte limit, not both.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The bounded read supplies one supported limit form and returns a page within the captured policy.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Context admission, storage and reading are separate from executing a tool mutation. Preserve existing task state and receipts; a context diagnostic does not authorize replay of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
